review.why: Audit application trust boundaries with evidence-backed findings, independent verification and structured reports.
review.summary: Defines a six-phase source audit with coverage tracking, domain references and two tested validators for findings and audit coverage.
strengths: Complete workflow with explicit evidence and incomplete-run rules.
All bundled text, validator code and tests read; 65 validator tests pass in isolated Linux.
Separates confirmed findings, unresolved hypotheses and rejected candidates.
cautions: The validator CLIs reject inputs on the tested native Windows runtime; Linux is required for the tested path.
Full audits need tool-capable models, parallel agents and an OS-enforced sandbox, with an explicit work budget.
Validator tests check report correctness, not the effectiveness of a full audit at discovering vulnerabilities.
